title: Private Deploy Release Runbook — Image Signing & Terraform Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for private deployment release mechanics focused on three correlated areas: Terraform module lifecycle for infra manifests, GitOps/ArgoCD release patterns for Helm-based apps, and end-to-end image signing/attestation for air-gapped or VPC-hosted clusters. Goal is to capture concrete checklists, failure modes, and small runnable commands we can paste into CI pipelines or run manually during cutovers.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target environments: customer VPCs (managed control-plane) and on-prem clusters (air-gapped registries).
- We assume an internal image registry mirror is available for air-gapped installs (registry.redwood-mirror.local).
- We use cosign for signing images, Notation/fulcio for attestation, and a k8s admission controller (image-policy-webhook) to enforce signatures.
- Terraform modules live in infra-modules repo and are versioned with tags; application Helm charts live in charts/ and are published to our internal Helm repo for private deployments.

High-level release flow (single release):
1) Developer/SE opens a release PR for the app chart + values in private-deployments repo. PR must include: Helm chart version bump, values (customer or env-specific), and image digests (not :latest).
2) CI runs: lint (helm lint), chart tests (ct), unit smoke (k8s-kind helm install), and image verification step that checks image digest exists in our mirror and has a valid cosign signature.
3) If CI green, PR is merged -> Git tag for the chart is created by CI -> ArgoCD picks up change in the customer Git repo (gitops).
4) ArgoCD executes a staged rollout according to the env's rollout policy: canary percentages or blue/green via Helm hooks.
5) Post-rollout, an infra Terraform change (if needed) is applied by our infra pipeline. Terraform changes are gated by a plan review and signed state locking.

Detailed checks and commands (copyable):
- Verify image present in mirror and digest:
  curl -s -u ci-token:$REG_TOKEN "https://registry.redwood-mirror.local/v2/$REPO/manifests/$DIGEST" | jq -r '.config.digest'
- Cosign signature verification (public-key mode):
  COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE@sha256:$DIGEST
- Offline signature attestation check (attestation bundle):
  cosign verify-attestation --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY --predicate /tmp/predicate.json $IMAGE@sha256:$DIGEST

CI pipeline extensions (recommendations):
- Step: image-signature-check (fails build if missing or unverifiable). Uses short-circuit and posts comment to PR with failure reason and remediation link.
- Step: chart-value-sanity — validate that required customer secrets are templated as k8s secrets references and not inlined.
- Step: terraform-diff — run terraform plan with a stable backend (S3-with-locking) and attach plan output to PR for reviewer.

Terraform module lifecycle notes (issues we've hit + mitigation):
- Problem: module drifting because teams vendor modules and forget upstream fixes.
  Mitigation: Add a small tfscript in CI that runs `tfmigrate` compatibility checks and fails if local module sources diverge from registry versions.
- Problem: state conflicts during concurrent infra updates for the same customer.
  Mitigation: Stronger state locking (DynamoDB lock table) + an explicit `release` claim step in Jenkins/CI to acquire lock before apply. Document each apply with a short commit to infra-ops-log in the customer's git repo.
- Version pinning: enforce module versions in terraform.tfvars and check in pre-merge hook. Provide an automated bump PR generator for patch upgrades.

ArgoCD and Helm upgrade patterns (recommended):
- Use image digest pins in the Helm values: image.tag: <sha256:...> and image.pullPolicy: IfNotPresent for airgap clusters.
- Rollout strategy: prefer progressive canary via Argo Rollouts when the chart exposes probe endpoints. If not available, use Helm pre/post hooks + weighted services.
- Emergency rollback: keep last-known-good HelmRelease in a special branch `releases/stable/<customer>` and promote that branch if rollback required. For faster reverts, attach a `rollback.sh` script that sets the HelmRelease annotation `argocd.argoproj.io/force-sync: \"true\"` and applies the previous Kustomize overlay.

Image signing and attestation specifics:
- Signing process (CI): after image build -> push to staging mirror -> cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY $IMAGE@sha256:$DIGEST -> upload signature to registry (cosign does this automatically for OCI registries) -> publish attestation blob to TUF mirror for airgap.
- In air-gapped installs: we mirror signatures and attestations to registry.redwood-mirror.local and store public keys in cluster via sealed-secrets (encrypted for customer cluster KMS).
- Admission enforcement: image-policy-webhook configured with trusted public keys; failure modes: webhook denying deployments must surface a clear error pointing to cosign verification step in CI.

Air-gap/Offline installation edge-cases:
- Container images built by customer: document how to sign with our public key and register the signature; provide a small helper: `redwood-attest sign --key cosign.key --image registry/customer/repo:tag` that wraps cosign but enforces metadata schema.
- Registry pull-through cache warmup: before cutover, run a registry-warmup job (list of digests from Helm values -> docker pull -> docker push to mirror) and verify all digests present.

Pre-release checklist (manual run for first-of-kind customer or major upgrade):
- [ ] Run terraform plan and attach human-readable diff to the PR.
- [ ] Confirm all image digests in values.yaml are present in the mirror and cosign-verified.
- [ ] Confirm chart manager bumped chart version and CT passed.
- [ ] Confirm ArgoCD target cluster has public keys mounted and admission controller deployed.
- [ ] Confirm rollback branch exists and `releases/stable/<customer>` is healthy.
- [ ] Run smoke e2e tests in an isolated staging cluster that mirrors the customer's node OS and kube-distro.

Postmortem triggers (what warrants an incident):
- Rollout causes >1% customer traffic errors or SLA violations for >10 minutes.
- Image signature verification issues across >1 cluster in the same time window.
- Terraform state corruption or loss.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we require a signed attestation for all base images (alpine/ubuntu) or only Redwood-built images? Need security policy clarification.
- Should we centralize public key rotation to a single operator, or allow per-customer key pairs stored as sealed-secrets? Trade-offs: rotation complexity vs blast radius.
- Investigation: evaluate Notation + Nexus integration as an alternative to cosign for better enterprise key management.

Quick links and references:
- Internal image signing how-to (draft): github.com/redwood-internal/docs/image-signing-draft
- ArgoCD progressive rollout pattern example repo: github.com/redwood-inference/argocd-rollouts-examples
- Terraform modules registry: https://modules.redwood-internal.local/

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and contains command snippets we expect to iterate. Please add missing failure scenarios you have seen in customer installs, especially around registry mirror drift and sealed-secret decrypt issues. If we agree on the signature policy, we can convert the verified steps into required CI gates and update the ArgoCD admission config templates.
